ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, S.C. 2000, c. 17, as amended; Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Regulations, SOR/2002-184; Alberta Business Corporations Act, R.S.A. 2000, c. B-9, ss. 114.1–114.4 (transparency/UBO register); FINTRAC Beneficial Ownership and Politically Exposed Persons Compliance Directives.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Passport bio-data page of each director and ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport authority of the applicant's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization (for non-Hague states)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address (utility invoice or bank statement under 3 months old)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or regulated bank in the applicant's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized copy transmitted with Hague Apostille

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency / Corporate Good Standing (where a corporate UBO is named)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign corporate registry / registered agent in the corporate UBO's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Beneficial Ownership Declaration and Authorization form (UBO register worksheet)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization in Canada (no apostille required for domestic document)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory FINTRAC risk-based screening of all directors, shareholders, and authorized signatories against the Canadian Consolidated Autonomous Sanctions List, United Nations Security Council sanctions, RCMP/CSIS watchlists, and, for cross-border e-commerce/payment integration, the U.S. OFAC SDN List. Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) and family members or close associates require enhanced due diligence, source-of-wealth verification, and senior-management approval prior to incorporation.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry (Government of Alberta, operated by Service Alberta and accessible through the Alberta Canada Corporate Registry portal)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A proposed corporate name must be expressed in English or French using the Roman alphabet; numbers and punctuation are limited according to the Alberta Corporate Registry Name Policy. Non-Latin characters require a verified transliteration and may be refused where the transliteration creates confusion with an existing Alberta name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the proposed name is rejected by the Alberta Corporate Registry, the applicant or incorporator may file a written request for reconsideration with Service Alberta Corporate Registry within 30 days of the rejection, annexing a new NUANS-style name search report and supporting arguments. If the Registry maintains the refusal, judicial review may be pursued before the Court of King's Bench of Alberta within 60 days.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible subject to strict conditions: the registered office must be a physical address in Alberta at which legal process and corporate notices can be served during business hours; a professional virtual-office service provider with desk space and mail handling can satisfy this obligation. Pure non-physical mailboxes are not permitted. An automated dropshipping model with no Alberta physical operational presence is tolerated for name and registered-office compliance but may heighten substance review by banks, payment processors, and tax authorities.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate: approximately 15% probability that the Alberta registry, anti-money-laundering regulator, or municipal licensing authority performs an unannounced physical inspection during the first 24 months for an online retail/dropshipping ULC; probability rises to 30% where non-resident UBOs, frequent changes in payment rails, or high-volume cross-border payment flows are identified.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office address service (virtual physical office, first 3 months)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registered agent / commercial virtual office provider in Alberta
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for physical-address mail-handling service

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: PEP/UBO sanctions screening software and OFAC/UN list checks (per 5 individuals)
Notarization, apostille, and consular legalization of foreign identity/UBO documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing notarial tariff and fixed consular fees

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c. B-9, as amended, including articles of incorporation, unlimited liability corporation status, registered office, and organizational requirements under sections 6-16 and applicable ABCA regulations.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Corporate Registry Service, Service Alberta and Red Tape Reduction
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Form 1) and Certificate of Incorporation
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is imposed on an Alberta ULC. Shares may be issued for lawful consideration as set by the directors; no escrow deposit or paid-up capital account is required for a non-distributing (private) unlimited liability corporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: BE IT RESOLVED AS THE FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF THE CORPORATION: (1) The Articles of Incorporation filed with the Alberta Corporate Registry are accepted and the Certificate of Incorporation received is recorded in the corporate minute book. (2) The registered office of the Corporation is established as [Registered Office Address, Alberta] and written notice is authorized for filing. (3) The initial share subscriptions are approved, and shares are issued to the founding subscribers named in the subscription list, with each subscriber acquiring an unlimited liability status under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta). (4) The following officers are appointed: [Name], Chief Executive Officer; [Name], Corporate Secretary, to serve at pleasure until the first annual general meeting.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry via accredited registry Agent or NUANS online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File an electronic NUANS name search request for up to three proposed corporate names containing 'Unlimited Liability Corporation' or 'ULC'. Review the NUANS report, which remains valid for 90 days, and select a name that does not conflict with previously registered names or trademarks.
required_dossiers: Applicant contact information for the registry agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected due to confusion or offence, either file a new NUANS search and resubmit within 10 business days or incorporate as a numbered company under a name such as '1234567 Alberta Unlimited Liability Corporation', which does not require a name approval.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare and file Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (electronic filing through an accredited registry Agent)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete Form 1 (Articles of Incorporation), setting out the share capital structure, the unlimited liability provision, and the initial registered office address in Alberta. Obtain signed consents from all initial directors. Submit the articles electronically together with the NUANS report and required statutory declarations, and pay the provincial filing fee.
required_dossiers: Consent to act as director (each initial director)
Notice of registered office (if not included in articles)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry returns a defect notice for an incomplete filing, remedy the stated omission within 15 days by filing a corrected page or consent; no further NUANS fee is charged for ministerial corrections.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Receive Certificate of Incorporation and confirm ULC status
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval and fee settlement, the Corporate Registry will issue a Certificate of Incorporation. Verify that the certificate indicates 'unlimited liability corporation' status and record the certificate in the corporate minute book.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate is delayed more than three business days, contact the Corporate Registry help desk. Any typographical error on the certificate may be cured by submitting a Form 1 Reconsideration or Alternate Report with corrected data.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Hold statutory organizational meeting and adopt first board resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of directors / incorporators and the registered office of the Corporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene an organizational meeting of the incorporators or directors. Adopt the first board resolution accepting shares, designating the registered office, and appointing the inaugural officers. Execute the resolution in writing and file it in the corporate minute book.
required_dossiers: First board resolution incorporating share subscription and office appointments
Consent of each officer to act
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If an omission in the organizational records is discovered, adopt a supplemental unanimous written resolution signed by all directors, which is permissible under the ABCA.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-formation CRA business number and municipal/occupational clearances
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (Business Registration Online) and Alberta municipal licensing offices
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the federal Business Number through Business Registration Online, attaching the corporate numbered information. Register for GST/HST if expected annual taxable supplies exceed C$30,000. If a physical office or warehouse will be operated, confirm municipal business licensing and zoning clearance; otherwise record an online-only operational exemption.
required_dossiers: Corporate mailing address and directors' identification
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA rejects the registration because of information mismatch, correct the registry data and resubmit. If the municipal authority requires a physical-precincts licence, apply under the City of Calgary/Edmonton general business licence class, or request a written exemption for remote operations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — no industrial licensing authority exists in Alberta for ISIC 4791 (automated dropshipping retail). A separate municipal business licence will only be required if a physical office, warehouse, or storage site is opened in a municipality.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable — no manufacturing, processing, or operational permit is required for an automated dropshipping network operated solely through e-commerce platforms.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Alberta Environment and Protected Areas (AEPA) — not applicable to an online retail automated dropshipping service.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — no EIA registration, screening or full assessment is triggered because there is no physical construction, manufacturing, wastewater discharge or air emission.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial discharge or VOC emission thresholds apply. General duty to comply with Municipal Government Act wastewater/sanitary sewers bylaws and Alberta's environmental protection standards applies if an office lease is signed; e-waste (unusable electronics) is handled under provincial recycling regulations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not required for a purely virtual dropshipping operation. If the company later leases office or warehouse space, Alberta OHS Code, fire safety inspection, municipal building permits, and structural load certification will be mandatory before occupancy.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency / Agence du revenu du Canada (CRA) — official portal: https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency.html; Alberta provincial registry — Service Alberta Corporate Registry, portal: https://www.alberta.ca/corporate-registry.aspx; Alberta corporate income tax is administered by CRA under a tax-collection agreement.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a non-resident-owned Alberta ULC: (1) incorporate through Service Alberta Corporate Registry and obtain the Alberta corporate access number; (2) apply to CRA on Form RC1 (Request for a Business Number and Certain CRA Program Accounts) or through Business Registration Online; (3) CRA issues the 9-digit Business Number (BN) as the statutory tax identifier; (4) the same BN is used for the corporate income tax account ('RP') and, where required, the GST/HST account ('RT'), payroll ('RC'), and other CRA program accounts. A foreign resident without a Canadian Social Insurance Number may submit the RC1 by mail or fax with certified copies of incorporation documents and officer identification.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible (an Alberta ULC is eligible for U.S. check-the-box pass-through/disregarded classification; under Canadian Income Tax Act Part I the entity remains a separate taxable corporation on its worldwide income, and no Canadian partnership pass-through is available).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: U.S. check-the-box election under IRS Form 8832 can be made to treat the Canadian ULC as a corporation, partnership, or disregarded entity for U.S. federal tax purposes; no similar election exists under Canadian domestic law. Any hybrid mismatch benefit is subject to Canadian anti-hybrid rules and U.S. GILTI, BEAT, and CFC limitations.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST (Goods and Services Tax) under Part IX of the Excise Tax Act; Alberta has no provincial sales tax and does not participate in the HST.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: $30,000 CAD of consideration from taxable supplies made in Canada in the current calendar quarter and the four preceding calendar quarters; registration becomes mandatory once the supplier ceases to be a 'small supplier' under the Excise Tax Act. Voluntary registration is available below this threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, CRA API stamping, or government pre-approval of invoices exists in Canada. GST/HST registrants must issue complete electronic invoices and retain records; GST/HST returns are filed electronically via NETFILE. For exports, CBSA receives electronic export/cargo data (ACI/eManifest) but does not approve commercial invoices before shipment.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A supply of tangible personal property may be zero-rated under Schedule VI, Part V of the Excise Tax Act when the goods are physically exported by or on behalf of the supplier, ownership passes outside Canada, and contemporaneous commercial and customs documentation proves export. Services and intangible personal property supplied to a non-resident may be zero-rated if the service or intangible is supplied wholly outside Canada or is not for use in Canada, subject to statutory exclusions for real property in Canada, tangible personal property ordinarily located in Canada, and services rendered to individuals physically present in Canada.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (CBSA Form B13A or approved electronic export declaration where applicable)
Bill of Lading / Waybill (original or electronic carrier document showing destination outside Canada)
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank wire-transfer record evidencing payment from the export buyer within 180 days
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA audits export zero-rating claims under the GST/HST and may disallow the 0% rate if the exporter fails to maintain or produce the required documentary bundle, causing a retroactive assessment of 5% GST/HST plus daily compound interest. The normal four-year reassessment period is extended in cases of misrepresentation or fraud. Civil penalties include false-statement and gross-negligence penalties; CRA may claw back refunds already paid and recommend criminal prosecution for wilful evasion.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada), in coordination with the Department of Finance Canada for currency policy and the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) for federally regulated banking supervision; anti-money-laundering supervision is exercised by the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains fully free capital and current account convertibility under the Currency Act, the Bank of Canada Act, and Canada's obligations as an OECD member and IMF Article VIII participant. There is no exchange-control licensing requirement, no restriction on conversion of CAD, and no prior authorization for dividend, profit, or capital repatriation. Cross-border payments remain subject to FINTRAC reporting thresholds and the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA). An Alberta ULC may remit profits by eligible dividend or return of capital, subject to applicable non-resident withholding tax treaty relief.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada imposes no statutory export proceeds surrender regime. There is no mandatory timeline for repatriation of export receipts, no compulsory conversion ratio into CAD, and no requirement to maintain export proceeds in a designated account. Exporters may retain foreign currency in freely held accounts and convert as a treasury decision.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital EMI services have Low viability as a primary treasury rail in Canada because Canadian-dollar clearing ultimately requires a Canadian payment services partner or money services business (MSB) registration under FINTRAC. An unregistered offshore EMI cannot independently access Canadian clearing and settlement systems, and banks will generally reject settlement flows from entities without a Canadian regulatory footprint. Feasibility may rise to Medium if the EMI partners with a regulated Canadian MSB or a Schedule I bank and maintains transparent originator information on all SWIFT payments.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Canadian law does not mandate physical attendance for corporate account opening, but most Tier 1 banks require at least one director or senior authorized signatory to complete an identity verification interview, typically by secure video conference. Fully remote opening may be available where the Alberta ULC has a registered office, a Canadian director nexus, and a sufficiently detailed operating history. Enhanced due diligence applies to automated dropshipping, so banks will likely require a director or corporate officer to participate in interview and produce source-of-funds evidence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Automated dropshipping model characterized as high-volume, low-margin retail payment routing without physical inventory or seller nexus
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Alberta ULC incorporation certificate and Articles of Association; updated Alberta Corporate Registry extracts; beneficial ownership and director register; executed supplier agreements and app-based platforms; customer order data demonstrating merchant-of-record role; refund and chargeback policies; projected transaction volumes and average ticket analyses; detailed value-chain narrative.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border payment inflows from foreign payment gateways and marketplaces creating concentration of third-party settlements
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Gateway settlement reports from Stripe and PayPal identifying payout originators; reconciliation ledger matching platform payouts to sales orders; a master services agreement documenting the commercial arrangement between the gateway, the platform, and the Canadian ULC; evidence of Canadian economic substance including registered office, bank mandate, accounting records, and board decision-making files.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Chargebacks and potential card-not-present fraud on target payment rails raising AML and merchant integrity concerns
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PCI DSS compliance certificate; activation records for 3D Secure, AVS, and CVV checks; chargeback mitigation policy; transaction velocity and merchant fraud rules; sanctions screening procedures; FINTRAC suspicious transaction reporting protocol; appointment of a compliance officer responsible for ongoing AML training and monitoring.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: ULC pass-through eligibility and non-resident ownership causing tax re-characterization or unclear ultimate beneficial ownership
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Canadian tax opinion on entity classification of an unlimited liability corporation under the Income Tax Act; statutory unlimited liability language; indemnification and pledge agreements with non-resident shareholders; shareholder resolutions authorizing accounts; personal identification of all directors and beneficial owners; signed declarations confirming Canadian source income reporting obligations.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections to the Alberta ULC should be routed by SWIFT International Wire with a clear payment narrative referencing the corporate resolution and the purpose of the remittance. Recommended labels include 'capital contribution', 'shareholder loan', or 'working capital advance' under a written funding agreement. Because Canada has no exchange control approval system, no prior central bank filing is required, but the receiving bank will apply enhanced verification, and all international wires over CAD 10,000 are reportable to FINTRAC. Foreign-currency inbound transfers can be converted to CAD freely at commercial FX rates.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements are typically cleared by SWIFT MT103 customer credit transfers for high-frequency, low-value supplier and logistics payments, and by commercial documentary letters of credit for bulk inventory purchases. The ULC may freely choose settlement currency. All outbound SWIFT transactions over CAD 10,000 trigger FINTRAC EFT reporting, and sanctions screening obligations must be satisfied before any payment. CAD conversion and disbursement are unrestricted.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: OTC FX outright forward contracts with a Schedule I Canadian bank or regulated derivatives dealer
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on freely convertible currency pairs for hedging non-CAD exposures
FX cross-currency swaps for treasury balance sheet hedging
Multi-currency operating accounts and natural hedging through matched foreign-currency receipts and payments

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary of date of incorporation; due by the last day of each anniversary month.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file for one year triggers administrative dissolution or cancellation by the Registrar; late filing may also prevent issuance of certificates and updates.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return, including provincial corporation tax schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) in coordination with Alberta Finance for provincial corporation tax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Six months after the corporation's fiscal year-end; payment due two months after year-end, or three months for Canadian-controlled private corporations qualifying for lower federal rates.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per full month of delay up to 12 months; repeated non-filing may lead to demand to file and prosecution under the Excise Tax Act and the Income Tax Act.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: GST/HST Annual Return (if calendar-year election made or below quarterly threshold)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Fiscal year-end of the GST/HST reporting period, six months after year-end for annual filers.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 5% late-filing penalty of the amount owing plus 1% per month to 12 months; compound interest on any outstanding amount.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No mandatory audit for Alberta Unlimited Liability Corporation based on revenue, assets, or share capital. An auditor is required only if any shareholder or designation under the Alberta Business Corporations Act requires it; otherwise the shareholders may unanimously consent in writing to waive the auditor appointment for each fiscal year.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian accounting standards for private enterprises (ASPE) under Canadian GAAP; IFRS permitted if the company is publicly accountable or elects IFRS in accordance with Part I of the CPA Canada Handbook.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Alberta has no annual a beneficial-ownership confirmation filing. An unlimited liability corporation is required to maintain an internal register of individuals with significant control, update it within 15 days of any share transfer or change in significant control, and provide it to enforcement authorities on request. The annual return to the Alberta Corporate Registry does not disclose UBO information.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control

stage_6.statutory_headline_rate: 23% combined general corporate rate (15% federal Part I + 8% Alberta general rate)
stage_6.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 11% combined small business rate (9% federal + 2% Alberta) on the first CAD 500,000 of active business income for a Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC); federal Investment Tax Credits; 100% CCA (accelerated capital cost allowance) for eligible manufacturing/processing and clean-energy equipment.
